newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - July heavy crudes mostly committed.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - July heavy crudes mostly committed.

text.p: Asian crudes were steady amid thin discussion, traders said on Friday.
Minas premiums were talked steady around ICP +25 cents per barrel for July, and were not expected to change drastically as most July cargoes have been committed.
"The July market for heavy crudes is almost finished," said a trader with a major oil company.
A Duri equity producer was heard to have sold 90,000 July barrels to an Indonesian affiliate at ICP +$1.00.
Traders were also waiting for Malaysia to issue its first sell tender for its Bunga Kekwah crude, likely out next week.
But the loading for the first Bunga Kekwah cargo may have been delayed to second half August, instead of first half August as initially planned, traders said.
A July cargo of Thevenard Island crude was sold at just over Tapis APPI +50 to a Hawaiian refiner on Wednesday.
A European major and a producer sold the last July cargo of Cossack and the last July parcel of North West Shelf respectively, although details of the trades were not revealed.
But traders saw limited upside to the light crude market, citing July availabilities of Harriet, Maui condensate and Tapis still on offer.
The first August Murban traded to Thailand, by a Malaysian trading company at Dubai +70, although the price and seller were not confirmed.
But rumours that a U.S. major had bought a Qatar Marine cargo either from a shosha or a European major at QGPC -50 or Dubai flat was heard denied by both sellers.

By market close, traders had tallied IOC's August buying tender as one VLCC of Escravos at dated Brent +1.20 c+f, a Gulf of Suez cargo at OSP +19, a VLCC of Qua Iboe from a trader at BQ +69.93 and a another VLCC of Qua Iboe from a major at dated Brent related price.
